newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Forrestania finds more nickel in W.A.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Forrestania finds more nickel in W.A.

text.p: Forrestania Gold NL said on Wednesday it had more encouraging nickel indications from drilling near the Maggie Hays deposit in Western Australia.

The company said a second diamond drill hole at the Emily Ann prospect within the Roundtop joint venture site, located three km north of Maggie Hays, encountered two zones of massive sulphide mineralisation of 1.05 metres at depth of 213.3 metres and 3.3 metres at a depth of 234.1 metres.
Assays were not yet available but the zones are similar to intersections announced last week and would typically assay in excess of four percent nickel, Forrestania said.

Forrestania reported on February 21 that the first drill hole at Emily Ann intersected 10.7 metres at 2.39 percent nickel with a broader zone of 14.7 metres at 1.94 percent. A zone of 0.85 metres had 8.98 percent nickel.

"The similarity between the intersections from the two holes at Emily Ann is highly significant, and indicates good continuity of the ore horizon. Drilling is continuing in the vicinity to further test the extent of and controls on the mineralisation," Forrestania's managing director, Barry Eldridge, said in a statement.

The Roundtop joint venture consists of Capricorn Resources NL with 25 percent and the remainder held by the Lake Johnston joint venture group which is equally owned by Forrestania and South African-based Gencor Ltd.
The Maggie Hays deposit is owned outright by the Lake Johnston joint venture, with the companies planning a bankable feasibility study in the Septembe 1997 quarter.
The deposit is estimated so far to contain 184,880 tonnes of nickel and 5,523 tonnes of cobalt.
But Eldridge said the results from a step-out drilling programme provided potential for a significant increase in the size of the Maggie Hays resource.

Forrestania said assays from two step-out diamond drill holes, located 300 and 400 metres respectively south of the Maggie Hays deposit, returned best results of 11 metres at 4.0 percent nickel and 22 metres at 1.1 percent nickel.
